the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
language: a system of words used by a community to communicate
Learning a new language takes years of steady practice.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
came: moved toward or arrived at a place or state; past tense of come
Help finally came after they had waited for nearly three hours.
back: returning to a previous place, position or condition
She promised to call him back as soon as she landed.
can: used to express ability or possibility
Anyone with an internet connection can join the online course.
survive: to continue to live or exist, especially after a difficulty
Few of the original buildings managed to survive the great fire.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
centuries: plural of century; periods of one hundred years
The castle has stood on the hill for several centuries.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
anyone: Anyone interested in the workshop should sign up before Friday.
speaking: saying words aloud; using a particular language
Speaking clearly is important during a job interview.
it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
home: the place where a person lives
After the long trip, it felt good to finally be home.
getting: the act of obtaining or receiving something
Getting used to a new city takes time and patience.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
hard: difficult; not easy, or solid to the touch
It was hard to concentrate with all that noise outside.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
hebrew: the language of the Jewish people, spoken historically and in Israel today
Hebrew is taught in schools throughout modern Israel.
was: past tense of 'be', used for the first/third person singular
Half an hour after a lesson ends, much of what was said is already gone.
written: expressed in the form of text rather than speech
được viết, ở dạng chữ viết
For centuries, Hebrew was written and read but rarely spoken at home.
read: looked at and understood written words
The letter was read aloud to the entire assembled family.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
prayed: spoke or recited words to a deity, especially as part of religious practice
The old chapel was still prayed in every Sunday morning by the villagers.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
almost: very nearly but not completely or entirely
She almost missed the last train home after the concert ended.
nobody: not a single person; no one
Nobody expected the small team to win the championship.
grew: increased in size, or became older
The small business grew rapidly over just a few years.
up: towards a higher place or position
Neighbourhoods with few trees and little open space heat up fastest.
had: past tense of have, used to show possession or a completed action
By the time she arrived, the shop had already closed.
scholars: people with deep knowledge in an academic subject
Scholars from several countries attended the history conference.
books: written or printed works with pages bound together
The old library holds thousands of rare books from past centuries.
continuous: happening without a break or interruption
The factory runs on a continuous production line around the clock.
tradition: a custom or belief passed down through generations
It had scholars, books and a continuous written tradition.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
did: past tense of 'do', used to form questions and negatives or as a main verb
She did all her homework before watching television last night.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
child: a young human being below the age of full physical development
Every child in the class received a new set of books.
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
asked: put a question to someone or requested something
He asked the librarian where he could find books on astronomy.
water: the clear liquid needed for life, found in rivers and seas
Soil and grass hold water, and as it evaporates it carries heat away.
distinction: a clear difference between two things
There is an important distinction between opinion and fact.
matters: In a job interview, first impressions really matter.
kept: continued to have, hold, or maintain something
The recipe was kept secret within the family for generations.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
studied: The disease has been studied closely for several decades.
used: past tense of use; employed something for a purpose
A language kept only in books can be studied but not used.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
words: It has no words for kitchen tools or playground arguments any more.
small: not large in size, amount, or degree
They live in a small apartment near the city center.
things: plural of thing; objects, ideas, or matters
She packed her things and left the apartment quietly.
kitchen: a room where food is prepared and cooked
The whole family gathered in the kitchen to cook dinner together.
tools: plural of tool; devices used to carry out tasks
It has no words for the small things like kitchen tools or playground arguments.
playground: an outdoor area with equipment for children to play on
The new playground has swings, slides and a climbing frame.
arguments: reasons given to support an idea, or disagreements
The debate team practised their arguments before the regional competition.
noise: a sound, especially one that is loud or unpleasant
The construction site made so much noise that nobody could concentrate.
door: a movable barrier used to open or close an entrance
Please remember to lock the door before you leave.
makes: A short walk after dinner makes falling asleep much easier.
because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
needed: The volunteers brought all the supplies needed for the rescue.
them: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the object
I called them yesterday but nobody answered the phone.
very: used to make an adjective or adverb stronger
The soup tasted very good after such a cold walk.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
late: near the end of a period of time, or after the expected time
They arrived late because of heavy traffic downtown.
nineteenth: coming after the eighteenth in order; 19th
The museum is housed in a nineteenth-century warehouse.
century: a period of one hundred years
The tradition has been passed down for more than a century.
group: a number of people or things gathered or classed together
A small group of volunteers cleaned the beach on Saturday.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
families: groups of parents and children, or related groups
Several families gathered in the park for the picnic.
decided: made a choice or judgment after considering options
She decided to move to the countryside after years in the city.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
chose: selected one thing from a number of possibilities
She chose to study medicine instead of law.
speak: to say words aloud; to use a particular language
He can speak three languages fluently.
their: belonging to or associated with the people or things just mentioned
The students left their bags in the classroom overnight.
children: plural of child; young human beings
The park was full of children playing after school.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
start: the beginning or first part of something
The meeting got off to a slow start.
other: different from the one already mentioned; additional
One shoe was blue, and the other was black.
option: a thing that may be chosen from a set of possibilities
Renting is often a cheaper option than buying for young families.
so: used to show the result or consequence of something
It started raining, so we decided to stay indoors.
became: started to be something, past tense of become
After years of study, she became a respected doctor.
first: coming before all others in order or time
She was the first person to arrive at the meeting.
native: belonging to a person by birth; learned from earliest childhood
English is not her native language, but she speaks it fluently.
speakers: people who speak, especially those who speak a certain language
The conference brought together speakers of over twenty languages.
roughly: The trip takes roughly three hours by car.
two: Two things mark it as worth keeping.
thousand: The children had no other option, and so they became the first native speakers in roughly two thousand years.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
missing: not present when expected to be; lost
Two pages were missing from the old book.
invented: The printing press was invented in Europe in the fifteenth century.
many: Many residents still remember the flood of that year.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'
The missing words had to be invented, and many were.
committees: plural of committee; groups appointed to perform a specific function
Several committees were formed to review different parts of the plan.
built: constructed, past tense and participle of build
The bridge was built over a hundred years ago and still stands today.
terms: words with specific meanings, or conditions of an agreement
The contract lists the terms both parties must agree to follow.
electricity: a form of energy used for lighting, heating, and running machines
The storm cut off electricity to half the town.
engines: machines that convert fuel or energy into motion
The warmth pouring out of engines adds to the city's heat.
office: a room or building where people do administrative work
She spends most of her day working in a small office.
work: activity involving effort, especially to earn a living or achieve something
The difference is not impatience on one side; it is what is doing the work.
some: an unspecified amount or number of something
Could you buy some bread on your way home?
new: not existing before; recently made, discovered or experienced
They moved into a new apartment near the city centre.
accepted: generally agreed on or approved of
The theory is now widely accepted among scientists in the field.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
others: other people or things not already mentioned
Some students finished early, while others needed the full hour.
quietly: in a way that makes little or no noise
She quietly closed the door so as not to wake the baby.
ignored: paid no attention to something deliberately, past tense
Her advice was ignored until it was too late.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
ordinary: normal or usual; not special or different
For most families, an ordinary weekend involves chores and errands.
preferred: liked better than the alternatives; chosen over others
Many readers preferred the original ending to the one in the film adaptation.
whatever: anything or everything, regardless of what
Some new words were quietly ignored by speakers who preferred whatever they already said.
already: before now or before a particular time
By the time we arrived, the meeting had already started.
said: past tense of say; spoke or expressed something in words
She said the meeting would start at nine o'clock.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
surprises: The plot twist at the end always surprises first-time readers.
people: human beings in general, considered as a group of individuals
Many people prefer walking to work during the warm summer months.
revived: brought back to life, popularity, or activity
The old tradition was revived by a group of young artists.
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
belong: to be the property of, or a proper part of, something
These old tools belong to my grandfather, who used them for decades.
using: present participle of use; employing something for a purpose
Once children start using it in the street, they bend it and borrow from other languages.
street: a public road in a town or city, usually lined with buildings
Children were playing football in the street after school.
bend: to make something curved or angled instead of straight
Workers had to bend the metal pipe carefully to fit the corner.
borrow: to take and use something that belongs to someone else, promising to return it
He asked his neighbour if he could borrow a ladder for the weekend.
languages: systems of words used by communities to communicate
The conference offered translation into five different languages.
produce: This factory can produce thousands of bicycles every single month.
forms: different types, shapes, or versions of something
Renewable energy comes in many forms, from solar to wind.
committee: a group of people appointed to perform a specific function
The committee will decide on the budget next week.
approved: officially agreed that something may proceed
The council approved plans to build a new public library downtown.
hardest: Learning to listen was the hardest part of the course for him.
never: at no time; not on any occasion
She had never travelled outside her home country before that trip.
vocabulary: the set of words known and used by a person
The hardest part of learning a language is often not the vocabulary.
coined: invented a new word or phrase
The term was coined by a journalist in the 1960s.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
afternoon: the time between noon and evening
We spent a lazy afternoon reading in the park.
done: Have you done your homework for tomorrow yet?
exactly: in a way that is precise or correct in every detail
A fact heard once looks exactly like one that will never be needed.
telephones: devices used to talk to someone in another place by transmitting sound
Old telephones in the museum still have rotary dials.
computers: electronic devices that process data and perform tasks
The school gave every student access to computers in the library.
cannot: used to say that something is not possible or not allowed
Visitors cannot enter the site without prior written permission.
reason: a cause or explanation for something
Nobody knew the real reason for his sudden resignation.
use: to employ something for a particular purpose
What cannot be coined is a reason to use them.
survives: continues to live or exist after a difficulty
The old tradition still survives in a few remote mountain villages.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
hear: It was too noisy to hear what she was saying.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
teaching: the activity or profession of giving people knowledge or skills
After years in business, he switched careers to teaching.
amount: a quantity of something, especially an unspecified one
A small amount of sugar can bring out the flavour of tomatoes.
official: approved by a person or group in authority; formal
The government made an official announcement about the new policy.
support: help, encouragement or assistance given to someone
The charity offers support to families in financial difficulty.
substitutes: takes the place of; uses instead of
Nothing substitutes for hearing a language spoken at home.
revivals: instances of something becoming popular or active again
Folk music revivals have appeared in several countries recently.
been: past participle of be, used to show a completed state or experience
They have been friends since primary school.
attempted: tried to do something, often without success
The climbers attempted the summit twice before finally succeeding.
since: from a particular time in the past until now, or because
He has lived in this city since he graduated from university.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
mixed: combined together to form one substance or group
The paint was mixed carefully to match the original colour.
results: things that happen because of actions or events
The test results confirmed what doctors had suspected.
lesson: a period of teaching, or something learned from experience
The teacher planned an interactive lesson about the water cycle.
seems: gives the impression of being something
It seems likely that prices will keep rising this year.
dictionaries: books that list words and explain their meanings
The library owns dictionaries in more than twenty languages.
lessons: periods of teaching, or things learned from experience
She takes piano lessons every Saturday morning.
enough: as much or as many as needed
There was barely enough food to feed everyone at the table.
lives: exists or continues to be used
A tradition lives only as long as people keep practising it.
inconvenient: causing difficulty or trouble; not convenient
The meeting was rescheduled to a less inconvenient time.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance
This plan works far better than the last one did.
harder: more difficult or more solid; comparative of hard
The second exam was noticeably harder than the first.
arrange: to plan or organize something in advance
Let's arrange a meeting to discuss next quarter's budget.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
textbook: a book that teaches a particular subject, used especially in schools
Every student needs a copy of the maths textbook this term.
